what: How each Pennsylvania place voted in five contests of the 2020, 2022 and 2024 general elections: the votes for the Democratic candidate or ticket, the Republican candidate or ticket, every other candidate on the ballot together and the total. Counties are the Pennsylvania Department of State's certified countywide returns; cities, boroughs, towns, townships and legislative districts are added up from the Department's precinct results, used only where they equal the certified returns of their county.
note: What this is: how the people of a place voted in that election. A county's figures are the Pennsylvania Department of State's certified countywide returns. A municipality's, and for 2022 and 2024 a state House or Senate district's, are the precinct returns the counties reported to the Department, added up here; those precinct returns are not the certified canvass (the official precinct returns are kept by each county board of elections), so a place is given for a contest only where the precinct returns of every county it lies in add up exactly to that county's certified figures, and is otherwise left out for that contest. Nothing is divided by estimate. Pennsylvania's returns carry no write-in votes, so the total is the votes for the candidates on the ballot. What this is not: it is not a prediction of any election; it says nothing about any candidate on a later ballot or about any voter; a nonpartisan office stays nonpartisan; and a district's figures are for its lines of that year. The candidates and tickets are named only to say which election this was. In a place with very few voters the split would come close to saying how particular people voted, so there the split is left out.

few.why: A place's too_few lists the contests in which it had fewer than 20 votes, or in which every vote went the same way. There the split comes close to saying how particular people voted, so a page should leave it out. The counts are the official record all the same, and are kept here so that the sums can be checked.

not_given: Congressional districts are not added up here (the congressional pages carry their own record). School districts and wards are not added up, and Pennsylvania elects no county, municipal or school office in 2026. Census statistical places that are not municipalities (villages and other unincorporated places) are not given: their figures are in their township's.

county.note: The Department of State's certified countywide returns, unchanged.

mcd.why_not: A municipality or district is missing a contest when a county it lies in has precinct returns that do not add up to that county's certified figures for that contest, and a district is missing a year when its own House or Senate contest that year does not add up to its certified result; nothing is divided by estimate.
mcd.note: A municipality (city, borough, town or township) is the precincts the Department's returns place in it, matched by name and county to the Census Bureau's county subdivision; one reaching into a second county is all of its precincts. Pennsylvania's precincts (election districts) never cross a municipal line.

house.what: State House districts of the 2022 plan (in force 2022 through 2030)
house.why_not: The 2020 election was held on the districts drawn in 2012; the districts drawn after the 2020 census were first used in 2022, so 2020 is not given. A municipality or district is missing a contest when a county it lies in has precinct returns that do not add up to that county's certified figures for that contest, and a district is missing a year when its own House or Senate contest that year does not add up to its certified result; nothing is divided by estimate.
house.note: Pennsylvania elects 203 Representatives and 50 Senators, one from each district; the Legislative Reapportionment Commission's 2022 plans were first used in the 2022 election and are the lines in force for 2026. Each precinct row of the Department's returns names the House and Senate districts it lies in, and a district is its precincts added up. Only half the Senate is elected each time (the even-numbered districts in 2022 and 2026, the odd-numbered in 2024), but every district has figures for every statewide contest on its lines.

senate.what: State Senate districts of the 2022 plan (in force 2022 through 2030)
senate.why_not: The 2020 election was held on the districts drawn in 2012; the districts drawn after the 2020 census were first used in 2022, so 2020 is not given. A municipality or district is missing a contest when a county it lies in has precinct returns that do not add up to that county's certified figures for that contest, and a district is missing a year when its own House or Senate contest that year does not add up to its certified result; nothing is divided by estimate.
senate.note: Pennsylvania elects 203 Representatives and 50 Senators, one from each district; the Legislative Reapportionment Commission's 2022 plans were first used in the 2022 election and are the lines in force for 2026. Each precinct row of the Department's returns names the House and Senate districts it lies in, and a district is its precincts added up. Only half the Senate is elected each time (the even-numbered districts in 2022 and 2026, the odd-numbered in 2024), but every district has figures for every statewide contest on its lines.
